entries.claim: The eval-command check only matches the literal words `claude`, `plugin`, `eval` joined by whitespace. Two ordinary ways of writing the command get past it: running the CLI through its package name, and a shell line continuation.
entries.failure_scenario: I ran workflowProblems on `- run: npx -y @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.327 plugin eval . --trust-plugin` and it returned []: `claude` is followed by `-code`, not whitespace. A `run: |` block holding `claude plugin \` with `eval . --trust-plugin` on the next line also returned []. The model-key checks don't make up for it. A workflow with `permissions: id-token: write`, aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK: "1"` reaches a model without naming `secrets` or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and the full text with the npx eval line also returned []. Such a workflow runs the suite in CI, and the guard meant to keep it out passes.

entries.claim: commandProblems only scans the one line that starts with `claude plugin eval`. If the README command is wrapped with shell `\` continuations, a `--case`, `--tag` or `--eval-dir` on a continuation line is never checked.
entries.failure_scenario: The README command is one line of about 180 characters, so wrapping it is a natural edit. I ran commandProblems on a section holding "claude plugin eval . --trust-plugin \" then "  --case fast-path \" then "  --no-publish" and it returned []. There is still exactly one line starting with `claude plugin eval`, and the filter on the next line never reaches the FILTER match. The test passes while the README command runs one case.

entries.claim: The test decides which cases the command runs by listing the top-level folders of `evals/`. `claude plugin eval --help` documents different discovery: it runs `<eval dir>/**/case.yaml` (recursive), and the eval dir is the manifest's `experimental.evals` when set. The test reads neither.
entries.failure_scenario: Case 1: a case added at `evals/readiness-fix/variant/case.yaml`. The command runs it, but readdirSync sees only `readiness-fix`, so the README can leave it out and the test passes. Case 2: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` gains `"experimental": {"evals": "evals-v2"}`. The unchanged README command now runs evals-v2/, while the test still compares the bullets to evals/ and passes. The test's own comment treats switching the folder as a filter, but it only catches the `--eval-dir` way of doing it. The coverage claim fails silently in both cases.

entries.claim: The SECRETS pattern flags the bare word `secrets` anywhere in a workflow, including comments and step names, which goes beyond the plan's "any `secrets.` reference". A correct workflow that reaches no secret can fail.
entries.failure_scenario: I ran workflowProblems on `- name: Scan for leaked secrets` followed by `run: gitleaks detect` and it returned ["secret"]. A comment such as `# no step sees any secrets` would be reported the same way, as "reaches a secret other than GITHUB_TOKEN", although neither touches the secrets context.
